title: Classification and accountability
instructions: Listen and select the words in the transcript that differ from the audio. Select a word again to remove it.
audioText: Automated classification acquires an appearance of neutrality when its categories are presented as purely technical. Yet the choice of a target variable already embeds a judgement about which differences matter. A system trained to reproduce previous decisions may faithfully replicate patterns that an institution ought to reconsider. Evaluating its performance therefore requires attention to the provenance of the labels as well as the frequency of predictive errors. Aggregated accuracy can conceal uneven consequences for groups whose circumstances are inadequately represented in the training material. Accountability depends on making these limitations legible to those affected and providing a practicable route for contesting decisions. The central challenge is not simply to increase computational sophistication, but to ensure that the purposes governing classification remain explicit, revisable and answerable to public reasons.
passage: Automated classification acquires an appearance of partiality when its categories are presented as purely technical. Yet the choice of a target variable already excludes a judgement about which differences matter. A system trained to reproduce previous decisions may faithfully rectify patterns that an institution ought to reconsider. Evaluating its performance therefore requires attention to the provenance of the labels as well as the frequency of predictive errors. Aggregated accuracy can reveal uneven consequences for groups whose circumstances are inadequately represented in the training material. Accountability depends on making these limitations negligible to those affected and providing a practicable route for endorsing decisions. The central challenge is not simply to increase computational sophistication, but to ensure that the purposes governing classification remain explicit, revisable and answerable to public reasons.

corrections.explanation: The system appears neutral when its categories are described as technical.
Choosing a target includes a judgement about relevant differences.
A trained system may reproduce questionable patterns rather than correct them.
A combined accuracy figure can hide unequal consequences.
Affected people should be able to understand the limitations.
A route for challenging decisions is part of accountability.
